Agent 13, Sharon Carter: Solid early pick, both hosts' top white uncommon. A 3/2 for 2W that Clues every time a creature swings alone (herself included) is a must-kill value engine, not raw aggression — the 59% GIH and +2.9 IWD are real. Best in WB attack-alone and any go-wide white deck; notably stronger on the play.
Agent Maria Hill: Solid early pick and a top-3 white uncommon. A 1-mana 2/1 that grows and draws every time you tap her for teamwork; the 59.8% GIH and 3.6 ALSA confirm she overperforms even outside a dedicated WU teamwork build. The broken preview hype cooled only because teamwork spells run thin, but she's still a first-pick-worthy value engine.
Agent of Atlas: Filler two-drop for the RW/WU prowess deck. A 56% GIH WR flatters the vanilla body — the negative IWD and 5.9 ALSA say it's a replaceable role-player that only shines when you're actually casting noncreature spells. Fine playable, not a card you prioritize.
Agent Phil Coulson: First-pick-quality GW signpost engine. A 1W 2/2 vigilance that pumps every other Hero each turn snowballs a wide board fast, and the 64% GIH / +9.4 IWD / 1.6 ALSA confirm it — taken early and wins the games it's cast. A must-kill anthem in the heroes deck; trust the live WR over the modest B.
Solid role-player exalted-in-white body that all three guides quietly like more than the D+ grade. The 55.6% GIH is real, but the -0.6 IWD flags it as a build-around, not a slam — it wants a WB attack-alone shell with a lone threat to pump. Fine 2-drop that scales in multiples.
Avengers Assemble!: Bomb in GW heroes. A flash +2/+2 anthem that also draws a card every end step you attacked with or played a Hero — that recurring card advantage is what pushes it past a mere anthem. 64.9% GIH / +10.1 IWD / ALSA 1.5 confirm it's a first-pick engine that snowballs go-wide boards. Beats its B+ grade.
Borough Backup: Solid role-player that punches above its C- grade — the 58.5% GIH and near-zero drawback (two 3/2 vigilance bodies OR a basic landcycle when flooded/short) make it a flexible mid-pick, best in GW go-wide and token-payoff decks. LR's 'should be higher than C' read wins.
Brave Brawler: Filler two-drop that overperforms its C- grade at 58.3% GIH — the lifelink turn-2 body matters when good twos are scarce, and the 4W power-up to a 4/3 lifelinker gives late relevance. A fine role-player in GW/WB heroes, not a priority.
Captain America, Super-Soldier: Bomb-adjacent and the WU/GW teamwork signpost. 60.9% GIH, +5.6 IWD and a 1.5 ALSA all confirm the shield-counter hexproof makes him and your heroes brutally sticky — near-impossible to answer through combat, and he protects your whole board. First-pick white, trust the live WR over the B grade.
Captain America, Wings of Freedom: Premium rare and a signal to be in white/GW heroes. 3/1 flyer with first strike and ward 1 for three is already above rate, and the attack-trigger anthem (+toughness to every other Hero) snowballs a wide board fast. 62.2% GIH at 1.5 ALSA and near-universal play — a bomb-adjacent early grab.
Captain Marvel, Earth's Protector: Format-defining bomb. LoL's 'garbage' preview badly misread this — she's a 3W 5/4 flash flyer with lifelink and an indestructible power-up, and the numbers confirm it (68.6% GIH, +13.2 IWD, 1.3 ALSA, A+). First-pick, splash-worthy ambush finisher.
Captain Mar-Vell, Space-Born: Marginal 5-drop flyer, not the payoff the mana implies. 4/4 flying vigilance is fine stats but the flash-while-opponent-cast clause rarely swings games, and a 54.3% GIH with -0.5 IWD flags it as a body that dies on cast like Serra Angel (LR/LLU agree, C/C-). Playable filler in white, not a priority.
Colleen Wing, Street Samurai: Textbook build-around: unplayable with zero self-targeting spells, a growing scry-engine with ~3+. The 55.3% GIH and 4.6 ALSA come from decks that support her (tricks, Falcon's Wing, Blazing Crescendo); the near-zero IWD confirms she's conditional. Take her if you're the tricks/RW-WU deck, pass otherwise.
Crowd of True Believers: Filler at best, near-unplayable per LoL's 'literal F.' A 1-mana 1/2 that only does anything in dedicated WB attack-alone, and the -0.6 IWD with 33% play rate confirms it's a build-around role-player, not a maindeck card. Skip unless you're deep in the attack-alone shell.
Helicarrier Strike: Efficient defensive removal and a white staple at 84.9% play — one mana for 2 (4 with teamwork) to an attacker/blocker. The 57.3% GIH validates LR's 'half a notch below unconditional' over LLU's C-; premium in WU/WB, softer in aggressive WR/WG that can't reliably trigger teamwork.
Hero in Training: A premium common: a 2/2 that cantrips unconditionally and gains 2 life beside another Hero. The 61.4% GIH and +3.5 IWD confirm the experts — you rarely pay four mana for a Merfolk Looter's worth of value on a body. Slam it in any white deck.
Invisible Woman, Sue Storm: Trap in most decks — the 46.5% GIH, -5.7 IWD and 30% play rate are damning. A 4W 2/5 lifelink that only pays off in a dedicated counters shell (or the Fantastic Four infinite combo) is dead weight elsewhere. Ignore the build-around ceiling; take it dirt-cheap only if you're already GU counters.
Jennifer Walters: Bomb mythic — take it P1P1. A splashable 2/3 for 1W (opponents can't cast on your turn is real interaction protection) that flips into a 6/6 reach/trample She-Hulk that pings. 64.9% GIH and +8.9 IWD is elite; the flip cost is a minor green splash any white deck can support.
Kree Commandos: Trap-adjacent filler. Lots of keywords on a 2/1, but one toughness means it trades down and can't block — the 51.8% GIH and dismal 20.8% play rate confirm the D grade. Only for all-in WR prowess, and even there it's a late add.
Luke Cage, Power Man: Polarizing WB solo-attacker that mostly disappoints. As a 4/5 indestructible attacking alone it wrecks removal-light decks, but the 51.7% GIH / -1.8 IWD / 39.7% play rate say it's often just a defensive 2/5 that doesn't close games — Alex's D+ read wins over LR's B-. Late playable, not a build-around.
The Mind Stone: A 2-mana white mana rock that fixes and ramps, with a late-game flicker sink — the +2.8 IWD and 1.9 ALSA say people first-pick it and it earns its slot. The flicker mode is mostly filler given few ETBs, so value it as a premium rock: good in any deck, not the bomb the mythic tag implies.
Mockingbird, Ace Agent: Trap. A 4-mana 2/2 double strike that needs you to spend spells targeting it before it survives — and it dies to any removal before the counter lands. 50.4% GIH / -3.0 IWD confirm the D grades; the double-strike ceiling rarely materializes. Sideboard/late filler only.
Monica Rambeau: Bomb. A {2}{W} 3/3 flyer with prowess that flips into a hexproof, team-pumping threat — 63.4% GIH, +10.1 IWD, 1.5 ALSA all scream first-pick. Near-unanswerable in a sweeperless format; take it over almost anything.
Murdock's Crusade: Real removal that outran its D grade to 60.5% GIH. Teamwork 4 exiles a toughness-4+ creature — exactly the enginey midrange threats that decide this slow format, unlike burn that can't. Sorcery-speed and needs bodies, but the WU/GW teamwork decks want a couple.
Fine role-player, not a rare-quality pick. In practice a {W} 2/1 aggressive one-drop that helps teamwork; the five-color power-up almost never fires. 57.4% GIH is respectable for a curve-filler, but the 61% play rate and C- reality say it's a body first, upside second.
Night Nurse, Healer of Heroes: Strong role-player and easy two-for-one. Flash lifelink 2/1 that regrows any permanent put in your yard this turn — even a fetched land makes it card-neutral, but it shines rebuying a creature that just traded or died. Flash plus lifelink gives it defensive flexibility; a comfortable early-mid white pick.
Okoye, Dora Milaje Leader: Premium white uncommon and a top GW go-wide pick. Three bodies for four mana with attacking-token first strike is excellent raw rate, and 58.8% GIH / 3.2 ALSA back the 'pure stats is incredible' read. Take early — it also fuels heroes and Okoye-style payoffs.
Origin of the Avengers: Strong, flexible GW two-drop enchantment. Scry 2, then either cheat in a ≤3-MV hero or draw, then an anthem — the 58.1% GIH and 1.9 ALSA (taken early) reward the heroes deck. Variable but never blank; a solid early pick that trends toward its ceiling with hero density. Trust the WR over the C.
Panther Pounce: Divisive one-mana trick that does four things at once, none decisively — no toughness means it's not a clean two-for-one, but you keep the Clue so you can't get blown out. The 54.2% GIH and low 28.7% play rate say it's a fringe playable; a copy or two in a WU/token deck, not a maindeck lock.
Patriot, Shield Wielder: Solid role-player, best in WU/tempo. A 2-drop with a repeatable +2/+0-and-hexproof pump is genuine threat-of-activation, but 'annoying ≠ good' — it can't protect itself and dies first. 57.8% GIH / 91% play rate says it's a fine early body that pulls its weight; middle-of-pack pick.
Political Triumph: The rare case where live data crushes the grade — D- on the tile but 60.2% GIH. A {W} turn-one snowball in a 16+ creature deck (scry + team-wide anthem payoff), a dead topdeck late. The high OH_WR (64.7%) confirms it wants to be cast early; solid in GW go-wide.
A build-around 3/3 tapper that punishes every noncreature spell — oppressive mana-denial in spell-heavy RW. But the flat 55.6% GIH and -0.4 IWD (67% play rate) show it's mediocre outside that shell; grade it C where a body-light noncreature deck exists, filler elsewhere.
Raft Security Officer: Filler tapper that overperforms its D+ grade — 57.9% GIH is quietly fine for a 1W 1/3 that repeatedly locks down a threat (cheaper vs. power 3 or less). LR's optimism beats LLU's dismissiveness here; a defensive playable in this slow format, and notably better against equipment decks.
Red Guardian, Super-Soldier: Clean removal-on-a-body and a fine white playable. Flash 2/2 that kills any creature that dealt damage this turn — technically play-aroundable, but as LR notes nobody on Arena respects it, so it functions as a two-for-one flash blocker. 59.3% GIH; grab it in the 3-4 range.
The Sentry, Golden Guardian: Overrated rare — the drawback is real. A 5/5 flying indestructible for four is a dream, but handing the opponent a mandatory-attacking 5/5 flyer that ~6 commons answer cleanly turns it into a coin-flip. The 53.1% GIH / -0.7 IWD say it's a mid B, not a bomb.
S.H.I.E.L.D. Spy Kit: Low-impact 1-mana equipment that overperforms its reputation. +1/+1 plus attack-alone untap/scry doesn't pay back the card (LR's D), but the 58.5% GIH and flat OH/GD splits say it quietly enables WB attack-alone and aggressive white. A fine role-player, best pick of the equipment commons — not high.
Super Villain Lockup: Premium white removal and a top-of-the-pack pick — flash exile on a tapped attacker, 56.8% GIH with +2.0 IWD and 91% play rate back the B grade over LLU's cautious C+. The 'tapped only' clause is the real limit (whiffs on defensive walls like Mr. Fantastic), but in a slow format most threats have to attack eventually.
Super-Soldier Serum: Below-average aggressive aura; the equipment rider is mostly text. +2/+2 first strike/vigilance is real tempo but you're two-for-one'd if they remove the creature. 54.0% GIH beats its D- grade slightly — it's playable filler in an aggressive white deck, not a card to prioritize.
Take Up the Shield: Top-tier combat trick that beats its D+ grade — the +1/+1 counter sticks after the lifelink/indestructible blowout, so it's a two-for-one, not a one-shot. 59.1% GIH backs LLU/LR's 'easy to underrate.' Play the first and second copy; best where your own hard removal is thin.
Wakandan Drone Flock: A 3/3 flyer with ETB scry 2 — an evasive body that breaks board stalls, which is why 57.6% GIH beats its D+ grade. Unexciting and the artifact type barely matters in white, but flyers are the format's tiebreaker; a fine mid-pick filler.
Web Up: Premium white removal and a high pick — the O-Ring catch-all every guide praises. 60.1% GIH with a 2.7 ALSA is elite for a common in a removal-scarce format; hits any nonland permanent and dodges the three-mana-removal downside by being 3 MV. Only knock: Guerrilla Gorilla can pop it.
White Widow, Free Agent: Flexible mid-pick that the guides split on (LR high, LLU low); trust the 56.0% GIH and slightly negative IWD — it's a solid role-player, not a bomb. The +1/+1-on-two-creatures or artifact/enchantment regrowth is versatile but low-impact for four mana. Reasonable body, take it midpack.
Aerial Doombot: Divisive one-drop flyer; the data lands it as fine UR filler, not a build-around. A one-mana flyer that power-ups to a 4/4 in the air is annoying and doubles as artifact + villain, and 57.7% GIH beats its D grade. Playable role-player, better than Alex's dismissal.
A.I.M. Scientists: Solid, flexible blue filler. A 4-mana 3/3 with ETB connive plus basic landcycling means it's never a dead card — smooths draws early, provides a body late. The 57% GIH belies the D- grade; it's the UB connive cycle's landcycler you actually want to cast. Late-pick glue, not a priority.
Atlantean Cavalry: Filler payoff body — a 3/2 vigilance that occasionally grows if you draw twice a turn. The 52.9% GIH and 27.9% play rate mark it as the last-few-slots card the guides call it; playable in a UB draw-two shell but very replaceable, pick it late.
Atlantis Attacks: Sleeper game-ender — but you want exactly ONE. Teamwork-4 lets a seven-drop bounce two things AND drop a 6/5 hexproof Leviathan, a backbreaking stabilizer in UW/UG. 57.0% GIH is strong for a common seven-drop; the gd_wr 59.1% vs oh_wr 53.5% shows it wants to come down mid-game. Second copy is a trap.
Attuma, Atlantean Warlord: Filler lord with a tiny tribe — MSH has few Merfolk, so this is mostly a 3/4 that occasionally cantrips on attack. 55.0% GIH and 45.9% play rate say it's a fine body but rarely exciting; a late-pick blue playable, not a driver.
Bold Biochemist: Unembarrassing 1/3 two-drop that blocks and draws two late via power-up. The 57.7% GIH with a positive GD/OH split confirms it's a synergy card, not a slam — best in UB draw-two where the counter-and-draw matters. Ben's "stinks" read loses to the numbers, but only just.
Bruce Banner: Strong mythic, treat as two cards. The front is a 1U hero with a repeatable X-draw that alone justifies inclusion; the RRGG Hulk flip is a hard-to-splash bonus. 60.7% GIH and +5.6 IWD off a 1.9 ALSA confirm it carries games even when the back never comes online. High pick in any blue deck.
Depower: Playable defensive trick, not a priority. For three mana (one if it targets an attacker) it's -4/-0 plus a cantrip — it neutralizes an attack and replaces itself but kills nothing permanently. The 6.4 ALSA and 45% play rate show it's a late pickup; the 56.4% GIH is fine for a cheap two-for-one in a controlling blue deck.
Echo, Perceptive Prodigy: Free value engine that mostly whiffs in practice. LoL loves that 'you do no work' — copy Killmonger/legend ETBs — but a 3-mana 1/4 with a fiddly tap ability posts a below-water 53.4% GIH and -2.4 IWD. Playable in UB grind decks, but easy to forget and rarely impactful.
Falcon, Winged Wonder: Premium blue uncommon and a clean two-for-one. 3U for a 3/4 flyer plus a legendary 1/1 flyer that surveils on attack is exactly the distributed evasion that breaks MSH board stalls — 60.4% GIH, taken at 3.5 ALSA. All three guides land B/B+; a top-3 blue uncommon and an early pick in any blue deck.
Falcon's Wing Harness: Sneaky-strong evasion enabler — free first equip granting +1/+1, flying, and ward 1, turning any ground body into a resilient clock. The 57.8% GIH and +2.9 IWD outrun the C- grade; LR's B- is the right read. Best as a one-of in blue-green to make chunkers fly, not an equipment-theme card.
Frozen in Ice: Premium-adjacent common removal for blue — one of the format's removal benchmarks. Taps, locks untap, and strips abilities, and NOT sending them to yard is upside vs graveyard decks. 57.7% GIH / 91% play rate; the only knock is no flash. High pick in any blue deck.
Futurist Forge: Build-around role-player: ETB cantrip plus a {3}{U} sac-to-draw-two. The 58.3% GIH looks fine but blue draws plenty elsewhere and this mainly earns its slot as artifact-count fodder in UR. Fine filler, not a priority — take payoffs first.
Giant-Sized Flying Ant: A 3/2 flash flyer with a minor tap/untap ETB — the flying keeps its GIH respectable at 58.0%, but the 51% play rate and D grades are right: the set wants cheap filler, not four-drops with no theme. Late evasive filler at best.
Hydraulic Helper: Build-around filler — only for a dedicated UR/artifact deck. A 1U 2/3 defender that taps for artifact-only mana is dead in most blue decks (35% play rate, 7.2 ALSA), but it curves you into the 4-drop artifacts. 54.9% GIH reflects its narrow home; skip unless artifacts are open.
I Am Iron Man: Fringe combat trick that wheels. Makes any artifact or creature a 4/4 flyer and cantrips — a blowout in combat or a surprise flying finisher, but it needs a board and leans on aggressive/UR artifact decks. 7.1 ALSA and 36% play rate say it's a niche late-pick; the cantrip keeps it from being a dead card.
Iron Lad, Diverging Destiny: Solid UR artifact enabler, mediocre elsewhere. A 3-mana 2/2 flying vigilance is a fine body, and top-of-library filtering into card draw is real with ~8+ artifacts. The 55% GIH is respectable; take it when you're in artifacts, otherwise just a flyer.
Ironheart, Clever Champion: Underwhelming rare that plays like a filler uncommon. A 4U 3/4 flyer is fine, but improvise and granting your noncreature spells improvise needs a UR artifact shell that MSH barely supports — the 52.5% GIH and 49.8% OH_WR (worst-in-hand) confirm the C-. A body in UR artifacts; don't pick it as a rare bomb.
Justice, Vance Astrovik: Bomb-adjacent uncommon and the format's best blue common-slot card — a 3-mana flyer that Man-o'-Wars a permanent and snowballs off your own bounce. The 63.6% GIH and monster +7.6 IWD confirm LLU's A-; tempo or value on demand, vicious with re-bounce effects. Slam it.
Kang the Conqueror: Bomb. A 4-mana 4/5 flyer is already premium in this slow, stall-prone format, and the extra-turn power-up is a real win-condition if the game goes long. 61.6% GIH / ALSA 1.6 confirm it's a top-tier UB signpost you take on sight — the body alone justifies it, the Time Walk is gravy.
Kid Loki: Build-around that needs the GU counters/rummager shell to matter — a {U} 1/1 that grows slowly on your second draw and hands out hexproof to counter'd creatures. 53.8% GIH and just 57% play confirm LLU-Alex's 'grows too slowly'; speculative, not a maindeck default.
Leader, Super-Genius: A bomb engine — 68% GIH, +15.2 IWD, ALSA 1.7 is elite. The 1/3 body doubles every connive into a free draw AND hands you a free connive each combat, snowballing card advantage instantly. LLU's "one of the two best rares" is right; a must-kill in UB, first-pick material.
Loki, God of Mischief: Underrated blue rare and an early pick — 58.8% GIH, +4.3 IWD off a 2.2 ALSA on a cheap 2/1 body. In a targeted-effect-heavy deck (removal, connive-tucks, pump) he draws a card nearly every turn; the format has enough targeting to keep him fed. Prioritize in UB/UR spell-y builds.
Mister Fantastic, Reed Richards: Build-around that stays on the bench without token support. A 2/4 reach for four is a fine blocker, but the draw-on-token-entry engine needs repeatable token-makers MSH barely offers. 53% GIH and -0.2 IWD confirm it's a giant spider with upside in most decks — only spike it if your pool is loaded with token generators.
Ms. Marvel, Kamala Khan: Build-around rare that slightly beats expectations in the grind. Drawing when you target your own creatures plus a hand-size power scaler is a real engine in slow UB/WU, but the 54.9% GIH is unremarkable and it needs support. A playable that overperformed its D grade; not a slam.
Multiversal Incursion: High-variance 7-mana build-around, not a bomb despite the mythic frame. Copying your nontoken creatures is game-winning with a fat board but does nothing off an empty one — the 51.3% GIH and grim 47.2% OH_WR (dead in your opener) earn the F, though it's a fine top-end you don't cut. Speculative curve-topper only.
Namor the Sub-Mariner: Work-intensive mythic that wants a merfolk/blue-spell density many decks can't reach — a 4-toughness flyer whose power and token engine only pop if you commit hard to blue. The 56.8% GIH with +4.8 IWD is respectable but not bomb-tier; ironically weaker if blue is contested. Good pick, not a first-pick-first-pack lock.
Pym Particles: Niche cantrip trick — a real card only in UW tempo/evasion. Free unblockable + draw plays smooth but is awkward when you just want the cantrip early. LR's B is overexcited; 52.3% GIH and 34% play rate back LLU's D read. Sideboard/synergy card, not a maindeck default.
Rewrite History: Trap outside a dedicated shell — 48.2% GIH, negative IWD, 17.8% play rate. The combat-tap trigger fights your own attacks and the payoff (return two instants/sorceries) is slow. LR's 'F on average, powerful built around' is right; leave it unless you're deep in a tap-value deck.
Secret Invasion: A premium removal-plus-threat aura at 59.6% GIH: exiles their best creature and turns your cheap body into a copy of it with ward 2, a two-for-one swing. Hits tokens too. Strong wherever you're blue; the +4.9 IWD and 2.3 ALSA confirm it plays like a rare.
S.H.I.E.L.D. Deployment Drone: The best common in the set per multiple hosts, and a fine P1P1. A 2U 2/2 flyer that brings a 1/1 is a genuine two-for-one that also counts as an artifact, a token, and a teamwork body — 60.1% GIH proves it. Flyers break this format's board stalls; multiples wheeling means blue/artifacts are open.
S.H.I.E.L.D. Flying Car: Strong rare and a high pick. Flash flying 3/3 vehicle with crew 1 that blinks your own creature — reset a tapped attacker, dodge removal, or re-trigger an ETB. 59.4% GIH and +5.2 IWD with 90% play; the flash flyer breaks board stalls and the blink is pure value. Grab early in any blue deck.
Shuri, Wakandan Inventor: Marginal UR enabler-payoff. Cost-reduction plus a clunky sorcery-speed artifact copy on a soft 2/1 body — the 55.3% GIH is fine but the copy ability is hard to exploit. A slightly-better-than-a-mana-dork blocker for dedicated artifact decks only.
Stature, Size Shifter: Excellent 1-drop mana sink for GU/blue counters. A 1/1 unblockable-while-power-≤1 pecks early, then power-up X ends games late — the 59.5% GIH with identical OH/GD splits shows it's good whenever drawn. Splits LR B / LLU C but the WR sides with LR; a great cheap play that fuels teamwork. Early-mid pick.
Super Intelligence: Trap/sideboard aura — you two-for-one yourself the moment they have removal, and the marginal 52.5% GIH comes from the rare games it sticks on a hexproof-ish body like Speedball. LR calls it an F for good reason; only a meme or a spot answer to a removal-light opponent. Don't maindeck.
Super Suit: Playable filler, best with artifact/equipment synergies. Flash auto-attach + untap and +1/+2 is fine tempo, but no hexproof and a middling +1/+2 keep it marginal. 55.2% GIH beats its D- grade; 27.6% play rate says most decks pass. Late pick that shines in UR/WU equipment builds.
Thirst for Knowledge: Artifacts-only card — 51.2% GIH and dead-flat IWD say that without artifacts to pitch it's just a clunky draw-two that dumps your action. LLU's D read holds; sideboard-to-marginal in UR, skip everywhere else.
Tony Stark: A mono-blue-friendly mythic that digs for artifacts on a 1/3 body, then flips into a 5/5 flying-haste bomb that cheats artifacts in. 60.6% GIH with +8.4 IWD and 2.1 ALSA — a strong early pick even without an artifact deck; the front half is fine card selection, the back half wins games.
Trickster's Stratagem: Underrated removal and a high blue pick — 60.8% GIH with a strong +4.3 IWD. Tucking a creature 2nd-from-top plus a connive answers bombs while firing your draw-two and counter payoffs; sorcery speed barely hurts since you want it on your turn anyway. LLU says A- if it were instant; take it as UB's best answer.
We Say Thee Nay!: Premium blue common — a scalable soft counter that overperforms. Quench base (pay 2), pay 4 via teamwork, and the mere threat taxes an opponent who taps out for the format's clogged four-drops. 59.7% GIH at 4.5 ALSA; Alex loves it and it plays well even held. A top-tier interactive pick for control blue.
Wiccan, Rising Magician: A 5-mana 4/4 flyer with a divisive forced flicker. In an ETB-value deck (UB/UR) it re-buys your good enters triggers, but the flicker is mandatory on noncreature spells and can misfire; can't blink itself. The 55.9% GIH says fine role-player — the flying body carries it.
The Wondrous Wasp: Premium tempo rare — near-format-warping in a flyer-heavy set. Flash 2/1 flyer that taps AND permanently strips a creature's abilities is a two-for-one that neutralizes a bomb while pressuring — 63.4% GIH, +7.7 IWD, 1.9 ALSA all scream first-pick. LLU's B- undersells it; trust the live numbers. Snap it.
Agents of HYDRA: Good aggressive 2-drop that's really two villains in one — a 1/1 that dies into a 2/1 menace, so it trades up and blocks well. 52.6% GIH with B- in villain-hungry decks; LR's 'don't sleep on double villains' is right. Solid BR playable, though few sac outlets mean what you see is what you get.
Arnim Zola, Bio-Fanatic: Below-rate role-player. Effectively a 2/3 body with a 3-mana-per-activation token engine you rarely turn on — needs 2+ creatures in yard and is slow. 50.4% GIH / -0.2 IWD confirm the D+ read; fine as a BG graveyard curve-filler but not a card to reach for.
Baron Helmut Zemo: Rare trap — BBB is brutal and the 3/3 body is atrocious, with the boast requiring an absurd 15+ black pips in your yard. 51.7% GIH and 43.9% play confirm LLU's D-; rarely worth playing even in mono-black-heavy BR.
Baron Strucker, HYDRA Overlord: A build-around that soured — LoL moved it DOWN and 56.4% GIH on a fragile 3-mana 2/2 that dodges combat confirms it. The villain cost-reducer plus connive-on-ETB is a real engine only in a dedicated all-villain BR deck; otherwise a do-nothing that dies. Speculative pick.
Black Widow, Super Spy: Premium aggressive mythic — a 1B 2/1 menace that can't whiff. The +6.6 IWD and 1.7 ALSA are the signals: every connection either grows her or steals a card, snowballing fast. Menace makes the damage reliable in the early aggressive turns. Slam it; the B grade undersells a card that ends games.
Construct a Cosmic Cube: Below-average enchantment; the 49.1% GIH and negative OH_WR are a red flag. The mind-control payoff at seven counters is a mirage you rarely reach, so you're really paying 2B for a slow drip of 2/1 menace villains gated behind drawing a second card each turn. Playable filler in a UB/Grixis draw-two shell, nothing more.
Crossbones, Malicious Mercenary: Below-rate BR villain payoff. A 4-mana 3/3 deathtouch that grows and pings only when villains flood in — the 52.9% GIH and D+ grade say it needs real villain mass to justify the slow, once-per-turn trigger. Playable in dedicated BR, filler otherwise.
Cruel Alliance: The best black removal common and a benchmark pick in the removal desert. Base mode exiles a ≤3-MV creature; with teamwork it exiles anything and gains 3 — Ethan calls it the format's best removal. 59.3% GIH / +5.6 IWD confirm. Sorcery speed barely matters here; prioritize it highly in any black deck.
Dark Deed: The format's best removal, full stop — a 1B instant -4/-4 that kills the 4-toughness bodies and clunky five-drops MSH is built around. 59.9% GIH, +6.8 IWD, 91% play rate all confirm the B grade is if anything low. Premium removal, first-pick material, splashable in any black deck.
Decoy Ploy: Marginal recursion glue, best in WB where it can grab both types. Two-mana instant regrowth is low-impact and does nothing early — -1.6 IWD and 24.8% play rate confirm it's a build-around, not a playable. Sideboard/late in a dedicated hero/villain shell.
Doctor Doom: The best card in the set. {4}{B}{B} for effectively three bodies (a 3/3 plus two 3/3 Doombots), self-sustaining indestructibility, and a card every turn — 65.4% GIH, +13.2 IWD, 1.4 ALSA. Bomb worth splashing or building toward; take it over nearly everything.
Doom Reigns Supreme: A high-variance villain payoff: 53.1% GIH is the format's verdict — great with 12-14 villains (drain plus two free spells at five counters) but embarrassing as a topdeck or in a thin deck. The 2.6 ALSA shows people overdraft it; only take it committed to BR villains.
Elektra, Daughter of the Hand: Bomb — the standout of this chunk. A 2BB 3/3 villain that ETB-destroys a power-3-or-less creature (killing most of the format) and can Sneak in for a flash ambush. The +11.1 IWD and 63.1% GIH are the highest here; removal-on-a-body in a removal-scarce format. First-pick black.
Grim Reaper, Lethal Legionnaire: Trap — reads better than it plays. A 3/4 for four with no ETB and a clunky pay-3B-on-attack reanimation that demands you attack into open mana with a fragile body. 52% GIH, 5.3 ALSA, sub-50% OH — the guides bury it (Alex D). A poor turn-five attacker; leave it in the sideboard.
Hour of Defeat: Premium removal — a takeable black catch-all. Unconditional instant-speed destroy plus surveil 1 for four mana, and 56.8% GIH / +3.9 IWD confirm it does real work. Slightly behind Cruel Alliance on rate but a high pick in any B deck.
HYDRA Infiltration: Grindy WB build-around sleeper, low floor. ETB discard-two plus attack-alone drain rewards the slow white-black attack-alone plan, but 28.5% play rate and 7.3 ALSA show most drafters correctly pass it. The 56.6% GIH is a conditional-inclusion number, not a slam. Niche payoff for a committed grind deck only.
HYDRA Troopers: Hyped then walked back — a 3/2 that only makes the tapped 2/1 menace with 2+ creatures in the yard, which it can't reliably enable itself early. The 53.2% GIH and split OH/GD (50.3 vs 55.0) confirm it's 'as good as your deck is': fine mid-game filler in any black deck, not a reason to be BG.
Kingpin's Enforcers: Role-player — a 2/3 lifelink villain with an overpriced 3-mana sac-to-draw. It's one of the few sac outlets, which matters in BG/BR grind, but the activation cost is too steep in a fast game. 54.0% GIH / 40% play rate: playable body, engine mostly aspirational.
Klaw, Sonic Subjugator: Premium disruption — a {2}{B} 2/2 whose ETB is a guaranteed, scaling discard (you choose the card, hitting harder as your yard fills). 56.9% GIH and B- validate LLU/LoL's high marks; a strong early pick in BR/BG that gives worst-case a body-plus-strip.
Madame Masque: A premium black uncommon and one of the set's best — 58.5% GIH undersells it. ETB connive plus a 2/1 menace token on every second-draw-per-turn snowballs card advantage and pressure; worst case a card-for-card connive body. LLU reaffirmed "maybe the best uncommon." Slam in UB/BR.
The Masters of Evil: Strong BR villain top-end — a 5B 5/6 that anthems your other villains +2/+1 for near-overrun, with a rarely-used plan tutor bolted on. 53.6% GIH understates it because the low OH_WR (49.1%) reflects a clunky opening hand; drawn later as a finisher it's a deck-ender. Take it as a villains payoff.
Bomb — the numbers scream it (63.3% GIH, +11.3 IWD, 1.6 ALSA). A 3BB 2/2 flying lifelink with pay-life connive to grow, and a static -1/-1 to every opposing creature that quietly wrecks the format's small/menace boards and enables your own combat. The anthem-down over-delivers; slam it P1.
Moonstone, Harsh Mistress: Connive-payoff role-player, weak outside UB grind. A 3B 2/4 flyer that recurs discarded cards is a fine defensive flyer, but the 51.8% GIH and 48.4% OH show it needs repeatable self-discard fodder. Worse than the other 4-mana 2/4 draw bodies; take late.
Ninja of the Hand: Mediocre BR villain body with an overpriced pump. 2B 2/2 deathtouch trades up fine, but the 5-mana power-up (discard + counter) is too clunky and telegraphed — 54.9% GIH with a weak 51.5% OH_WR and 51% play rate. Guides split but lean Ben/Alex negative. Playable deathtoucher, replacement-level, not a payoff.
Project Deathlok Soldier: Filler that doesn't do enough — a 1/2 with graveyard recursion but no sac, discard, or attack-alone home to abuse it. The 52.4% GIH and low 23.9% play rate match the D grade; it's an artifact-count body at best. Skip unless you're deep in a payoff that rewards the recursion.
Red Room Recruit: Solid 2-drop and key BG enabler — likely the only sub-4 connive common, giving free yard fuel plus a card. Ethan's 'great sleeper' beats Ben's 'small-ball'; 55.0% GIH / +1.8 IWD / 79% play rate side with the enablers. Good early pick for any black deck, premium in graveyard.
Robot Domination: Grade (B-) far outruns the 48.1% GIH and negative IWD — this plan only shines with your OWN sac outlets to trigger it at will; leaning on creatures dying in combat is too slow and the life loss stings. Build-around for a BG sac shell, not a generic playable.
Ronin, Shadow Stalker: A narrow equipment build-around — the 28% play rate and 55.2% GIH (from the few dedicated decks that ran it) tell the story. Pay-2-life equipment ramp plus sac-for--4/-4 is powerful only with real vibranium equipment; a prove-it card, mediocre filler otherwise.
Roxxon Brutes: Playable filler, better in BG than the D- grade suggests. A 4B 4/4 menace that occasionally grows on your second draw, with basic landcycling for flood insurance and graveyard fuel. 54.1% GIH is fine for a common curve-topper; Alex rates the cyclers higher for BG, and that's the read to trust.
Stolen Stark Tech: Filler equipment/trick. Flash it for a surprise indestructible + a marginal +1/+0 that stays behind — fine to blank removal or win a combat, but the equipped bonus is trivial. 6.9 ALSA and 39% play; only meaningfully good as a WB equipment enabler or with sacrifice. Last-pick material otherwise.
Super-Skrull: Strong heavy-black rare and one of the format's best build-your-mana payoffs. A 1BB 4/5 flyer alone is great, and each off-color mode (draw four, +4/+4, 4 damage, walls) is worth a light splash. The 59.4% GIH / +8.1 IWD and 2.3 ALSA confirm a premium pick.
Swordsman, Sharp Scoundrel: Dedicated equipment/villain build-around that needs the deck to exist. 1B 2/2 that attaches equipment on villain-ETB and connives on equipped attacks is a legit engine, but the 49% play rate and D+ show the WB equipment density rarely materializes. 55.8% GIH is a payoff-in-the-right-deck number. Speculative; skip in non-equipment builds.
Thunderbolts Conspiracy: Overrated rare that needs a villain count (~13-15) the slow format rarely delivers — a 4-mana do-nothing enchantment until villains start dying. The 49.7% GIH (below 50) and -0.8 IWD are the tell: it underperforms its C grade. Trap in most decks; only consider in a dedicated go-wide villains build.
Too Evil to Stay Dead: Trap/sideboard. Conditional reanimation with too much setup — ≤4-MV only unless you assemble teamwork-4, and it competes with better graveyard payoffs. 51.2% GIH / -0.7 IWD / 34% play rate confirm the D grades; neither host wants it. Pass.
Unliving Legionnaire: Below-rate flyer — a {3}{B} 3/2 that's a bad 4-drop and a passable 7-drop recursion engine only in the slowest games. 53.4% GIH but a 7.2 ALSA and 29.6% play confirm LR's D; a late flyer for grindy black decks, otherwise skip.
Visions of Villainy: Instant-speed Night's Whisper, usually 2 mana since nearly every black creature is a villain — but 53.5% GIH confirms pure card draw is rarely what this slow format wants. A fine glue card for control-leaning UB/BR, not a priority; leave it for the draw-two decks.
Whiplash, Vengeful Engineer: Niche role-player for black equipment aggro only. A {B} 2/2 that enters tapped and drains by equipment count — the tapped downside plus a 47.8% play rate say it's replacement-level outside its home. 56.4% GIH comes from decks actually caring about villains/equipment. Sideboard-ish elsewhere.
Widow's Bite: Solid black removal staple, cheap and flexible. -2/-2 at instant speed kills the format's abundant small/menace creatures for 1B; teamwork 3 upgrades to both modes (deathtouch + shrink) but that cost is steep. 56.1% GIH and 78% play — a dependable early-mid removal pick, and a combo piece with The Serpent Society.
Yellowjacket, Heartless Marauder: Above-rate BR two-drop and a good villains payoff. Plays as a 2/2 flying lifelink on offense when villains enter, and the format is starved for early flyers — 55.5% GIH / +3.9 IWD back Mark's B-. Solid early pick; just don't warp your draft to enable it.
Avengers Disassembled: Awkward but high-ceiling sweeper for UR/GR control. 3-to-each-creature is blunted by MSH's many 4-toughness bodies, and Stone Rain is a marginal mode, but choosing both gives flexibility — 54.7% GIH / +4.3 IWD earn the C+. A top card specifically in ramp/control shells; a sideboard-ish maindeck in aggressive decks.
Blazing Crescendo: Red's premium combat trick — a +3/+1 that replaces itself via impulse, so it's low-risk even in a blowout. The 52.2% GIH and 23.7% play rate mark it as a role-player, not a bomb; extra upside targeting your own creatures to enable Iron Fist/Colleen. A fine one-or-two-of in any red deck.
Crimson Operative: Solid red common — a genuine two-for-one in a format of one-for-ones. 3/2 prowess artifact villain that impulse-draws on ETB triggers three subthemes at once. Numot warns it's a value body, not a finisher, and it wheels; 54.5% GIH. Good playable everywhere but GR — take it, but removal comes first.
Death to Our Enemies: Build-around that misfires as a topdeck — 47.1% GIH, negative IWD, 24.4% play. The 7-damage payoff is real but the plan wants a turn-two start and a noncreature-heavy deck to ramp counters. Numot ran it in a spell-soup shell; niche RW/UR, not a default.
Evil's Thrall: A trap — 51.1% GIH and a 12.9% play rate are damning. Treason effects need sacrifice outlets to convert the steal into permanent advantage, and those are scarce in MSH, so you just get one alpha-strike back. The extended-duration villain clause rarely fires. Sideboard.
Fin Fang Foom: Solid RG/villain top-end on stats alone — a 2RR 3/5 flyer is well-costed and a flyer breaks stalls. The spell-copy engine rarely matters (Mark's read), so evaluate it as a 4-mana flyer that sometimes snowballs. 53.9% GIH is fine, not exciting; take it as a body, not for the ability.
Hawkeye, Master Marksman: Excellent rare, borderline bomb (LLU: could reach A). 1R 2/2 first strike reach that turns every tap into a pay-per-arrow menu — evasion enabler, reach-to-face burn, and looting all in one. 59.1% GIH, +6.7 IWD, 2.1 ALSA; super efficient and flexible. High pick in any red deck.
Hawkeye, Young Avenger: Build-around engine, weak standalone. A 3R 2/4 reach that adds its power to all your noncombat damage is Ethan's darling — Lightning Strike, Truck Toss, Repulsor Blast all go face — but it's a legend that folds to removal, and the 51.4% GIH / D grade say don't take it without the payoffs.
Hawkeye's Bow: Skippable equipment for all but the dedicated deck. +1/+0, reach, and a tap-triggered ping give no toughness and low impact — the 22.4% play rate, 7.4 ALSA, and D- are damning. The 53.3% GIH is pure selection bias from equipment decks. Effectively a sideboard card; don't main it outside a committed equipment build.
Hex Magic: Trap — a 3-mana discard-and-redraw that's card-neutral at best and actively bad when you're holding a bomb. The 45.5% GIH, -4.9 IWD, and 7.1% play rate are damning; the guides' F/D is correct. Do not play it outside a dedicated impulse-payoff deck that doesn't exist here.
Hire a Crew: Trap — every box it checks is too small. Token + team +1/+0 tries to do two jobs and does neither well; 46.1% GIH / -3.3 IWD / 6.2% play rate are among the worst in the chunk. LLU's optimism aside, the data is damning. Don't play it.
HULK SMASH!: Marginal removal-substitute — a modal fight/artifact-destroy that's awkwardly sized (teamwork 4 is a big ask) and best with deathtouch or prowess. 55.0% GIH and LLU's 'more constructed than Limited' read peg it as a C playable you run when short on real removal.
Human Torch, Johnny Storm: A 2/2 flyer that pings on each draw with another Hero — plays like a 3/2 flyer of reach in RW/RG aggro, but 52.0% GIH and flat IWD show it's fragile and conditional. The power-up is expensive. A playable evasive body, low-priority; needs a hero-dense aggressive build.
HYDRA Assault Robot: Solid filler that lives in UR/BR. A 1R 1/3 that pings on each villain/artifact ETB racks up chip damage where the triggers are dense, but is near-blank in GR (52.6% GIH reflects the mix). Playable defensive early drop with reach-into-late upside; take it when artifacts/villains are your lane.
Iron Fist, Living Weapon: Synergy trap in a vacuum — the 50% GIH and -3.1 IWD are damning. LoL calls it the best red card, but that's conditional on an RW self-targeting/untap shell; without spells to trigger it, it's a vanilla 2/3. Note the flip side: as LLU says, snipe it early when an opponent plays it. Only draft it if you're already deep in RW tricks.
Jessica Jones, Private Eye: Grindy card-advantage engine that overperforms in RW. Tap-and-stun to impulse cards equal to her power draws two-ish every other turn and pumping her scales it, and 57.6% GIH beats the C-. Understatted with no evasion, so she needs to stick — but a solid value pick.
K'un-Lun Warrior: Replacement-level red two-drop. A 2/2 with ETB sac-artifact-or-discard-to-draw is passable curve-filler but not a villain and awkward to enable — 52% GIH, -1.2 IWD, 33.6% play rate all say it's the last two-drop you'd run. Take it only when you're thin on the curve; C-tier filler.
Kree Sentinel: Serviceable curve-topper — a 5/5 reach villain artifact with landcycling flexibility, so it's never a dead draw. The 53.6% GIH and 57.1% play rate land it as the 'pushed solid common' LR describes over Alex's harsher D; reach matters against the flyers that break stalls. Late-pick playable, ticks villain/artifact boxes.
Lightning Strike: Your stock burn and a prime splash — the best red common, but temper expectations. 3-to-any-target trades up on the format's many 3-toughness bodies yet misses the 4-toughness creatures that decide games. LR's B vs the consensus C+: 55.3% GIH / 88% play rate land in between. High pick, not a bomb.
Loki Laufeyson: Solid spells-matter role-player — a {1}{R} 2/1 that copies your next cheap instant/sorcery (doubling a Lightning Strike is the dream) and can power up. 52.7% GIH is fragile/setup-dependent but LR's B is the upside; a good RW/UR pick, weaker as pure aggro.
Machinesmith Automaton: A near-trap: 50.8% GIH and 38% play rate confirm you won't hit enough artifact triggers to grow it. It's one of the less-embarrassing artifacts and a fine turn-3 trampler in a dedicated UR artifact deck, but never a reason to be in the lane. Filler, mostly cuttable.
Misty Knight, Hero for Hire: Role-player held back only by color competition. A 1R 3/1 is the set's only 3-power two-drop (great for teamwork/aggro) and a late-game rummager that pairs with connive/cyclers. 53.4% GIH and flat IWD say it's fine, not premium — LoL's "if it weren't red" captures it. A fine early beater in RW/BR.
Mjölnir, Hammer of Thor: Bomb-tier removal package (Alex A-/Mark A). ETB 4 damage kills most things immediately, equip doubles damage on your legends for lethal swings, and the 2R discard mode is a Pyroclasm-style board sweep. 59.3% GIH, +7.7 IWD, 1.5 ALSA — basically always playable as split removal. First-pick it.
Photon Blast Barrage: Better than the 'X-for-X' math suggests — a takeable RW/RG uncommon. Copy X times for 1 damage each mops up tokens and combos with Red Hulk (enrage) for ~15 damage. Bad into high toughness, so it flexes between maindeck and sideboard; the 55.9% GIH / +3.3 IWD confirm real utility.
Quicksilver, Brash Blur: Underwhelming aggressive rare — a fragile 1/1 with an expensive payoff. Free turn-zero start and haste are cute, but a 1/1 that needs a 5-mana power-up to matter dies to everything; 50.8% GIH / 49.3% GD_WR / 34.6% play rate confirm the D. No notes, but the stats are clear. Fringe RW aggro only; low pick.
Red Hulk: Polarizing finisher — a 6/7 reach trample with enrage that crushes red/green removal decks but folds to bounce and -X/-X. The 52.5% GIH and +2.2 IWD are middling because it's high-variance; the Photon Blast Barrage combo is the ceiling. A fine standalone beater in RG, not premium removal-bait.
Repulsor Blast: Serviceable removal that red needs to kill bigger things — below-rate at 4 sorcery-speed, but 5 damage hits most of the format and the teamwork face-damage rider saves it. 51.9% GIH sits between LoL's optimism and LLU's C-. A fine playable, not a premium; the gd_wr 54% shows it wants the board.
The Scarlet Witch: Build-around trap — the set lacks the big instants/sorceries to make her cost reduction pay, so she's a fragile 2/3 doing nothing. 47.9% GIH, negative IWD, 17.9% play all confirm D+; skip unless you've somehow assembled a heavy-spell UR/RW.
Speed, Young Avenger: A 2/2 haste that taxes you {1} to grant conditional unblockability — 53.1% GIH but a 32% play rate and negative IWD show it falls apart against evasion and isn't a villain. The early damage is real in RW spells-aggro; a marginal role-player, easily cut.
Stark Industries Executive: Filler ramp — a {R} 1/2 that pays 2-and-tap for a Treasure. Clunky (D grade, 42.7% play rate, 51% GIH) but turn-two ramp/fixing enables splashes and feeds UR Iron Man/artifact counts. Playable only when you want the fixing or artifact synergy; otherwise a weak body.
Super Speed: Near-unplayable — the 47.5% GIH, 8.4 ALSA and 5.5% play rate say almost nobody runs it. A one-mana flash aura granting first strike, +1/+0 and haste is a fragile two-for-one waiting to happen. Haste can steal a game, but this is deep sideboard filler for the most aggressive RW builds only.
Team Tactics: Scary but unreliable RW trick — a finisher, not a role-player. Teamwork double strike + trample steals games out of nowhere and pairs with deathtouch, but it doesn't protect your creature and the awful 50.1% GIH / 29.2% play rate show it's a build-specific card. Fine in dedicated RW, cut elsewhere.
Thor, God of Thunder: Format-defining bomb — first-pick, splashable. A 5/5 flyer that recurs an instant/sorcery/equipment on ETB and pings for spell MV on every noncreature cast is a Snapcaster on a dragon; 62.7% GIH, +11.6 IWD, 1.4 ALSA are elite. Best in RW/UR spells but wins any deck. Take it over almost anything.
Truck Toss: The biggest burn chunk — 4 damage to any target, cheaper with a vehicle. Guides split (Ben's #1 red uncommon vs LLU's C-), but 4 is the magic number in this format and the C+ grade with 67.8% play rate lands it as good, slightly-overcosted removal. High-priority in red; the RW/BR damage decks want it.
Vision of Love: Filler card-draw, mostly unplayable outside artifact-sac shells. Sac-or-discard to draw two is card-neutral-ish and does nothing to the board; 49.1% GIH / -1.0 IWD / 17.7% play rate confirm the D read. LR's Tormenting-Voice comparison flatters it. Sideboard.
Volcanic Villain: Filler at best — a vanilla 3/2 haste with an overcosted power-up; 49.3% GIH, 7.9 ALSA, 12.6% play. LLU's 'there's always a better card' nails it. Fringe aggressive filler you rarely want to run.
Wonder Man, Hollywood Hero: A trap flyer — 50.6% GIH and -1.1 IWD on a 5-mana 4/4 are below-replacement. The power-up doubler rarely fires twice, so you're paying five for a vanilla flyer that other cards do better. The evasion keeps it barely playable in RG, but pass it.
Ant-Man's Army: Excellent common and a high pick — Numot ran four. A 2G 3/2 that ETBs a Food or Treasure checks every box: ramp, fixing, splash-enabler, artifact-count, lifegain, tokens, all at a fair rate. Low ceiling but the highest floor of any green common; the glue that holds ramp/splash decks together.
Call Damage Control: Weak, narrow refuel — 52% GIH but a telling 14% play rate and negative IWD. Regrowing up to two permanents from the yard is pure late-game card advantage with no board impact, and it's worse than black's equivalent. Cut it from nearly every deck; sideboard grinder at best.
Claim the Kingdom: Trap enchantment — near-unplayable. Landfall spreads counters toward an indestructible payoff but stifles your curve turn two, forces the sac, and dies to exile/lockdown. The 50.9% GIH / -0.4 IWD confirm Mark's D-; leave it in the pool.
Doc Samson, Super Psychiatrist: Trap five-drop — a Doubling Season stapled to a below-rate body. 4G for a 3/6 that doubles counters and taps for X mana looks build-aroundy, but even in counters/power-up decks it adds little and clogs your five-slot — 52.9% GIH, -0.4 IWD. Both guides say D+. A late playable at best; don't prioritize the counter synergy.
Earth's Mightiest Heroes: Payoff mythic whose 58.9% GIH and +4.5 IWD come almost entirely from the teamwork mode — reveal 8 and dump every creature into play is a bomb, casting it fair is mediocre. The D- grade badly undersells the teamworked ceiling. Great in a WU/GW body-heavy build with power to tap; slightly bad if you can't teamwork it.
Epic Fight: Premium green removal, slightly underrated. Fight mode is efficient creature removal and the double-P/T mode ends races out of nowhere — the flexibility is the point. 58.3% GIH / +4.5 IWD / ALSA 2.3 confirm it plays above its B grade. High pick in any green deck.
Giant Growth: The bar for maindeck tricks has risen past a plain +3/+3 — 55.1% GIH looks okay but the 27.3% play rate and 7.4 ALSA show few decks want it. LLU's D- is the real read; a sideboard/one-of trick, not a pick you prioritize.
Go Nuts!: Premium green interaction — one-mana fight (plus optional counter) is a huge tempo swing, and 57.9% GIH with a C+ grade backs the experts calling it "nuts." Critical caveat: you need 3 power already on board to pay teamwork. Cheap removal is scarce here; a high pick in any creature-heavy green deck.
Guerrilla Gorilla: Fine filler with sideboard value — a 1G 2/2 reach hero that sacs to blow up an artifact or enchantment, one of green's few answers to Plans and to Web Up. 56.4% GIH is respectable; the reach and body mean it's never dead. Better in best-of-three; a fine last-few-cards playable maindeck.
Hellcat, Undying Vigilante: Greater-or-garbage: only good in heavy mono-green. GG 2/2 haste that returns as a 3/3 haste on death is fine value, but the double-green cost punishes any deck under ~10-11 Forests. The 56.7% GIH is a mono-green mirage. Notable as Killmonger sac fodder in BG; never a card to warp toward.
Hercules, Prince of Power: Solid RG/green role-player. A 3-mana 3/3 that power-ups into a 4/4 with vigilance, indestructible, and haste is a real threat-of-activation that's hard to block in the mid-game. The 54.9% GIH matches the C+ notes — a fine, unglamorous playable.
Heroic Feast: Once-a-format lifegain build-around, otherwise a trap. Food plus counters-on-lifegain needs a lifegain shell MSH doesn't support — 53.5% GIH, +0.5 IWD, 49.8% play rate, and LLU's D- all confirm it does little. The rare frame is a mirage. Leave it in the box unless you've specifically drafted lifegain payoffs.
Hulkling, Burgeoning Bruiser: Counter-factory engine that's just-stats without a home — a 2/3 vigilance that grows when bigger creatures enter. The 53.3% GIH and near-zero IWD confirm the guides' 'gradients of filler'; likely a 3/4 attacking for 3 on turn 4. Fine green playable, genuinely good only in a GU +1/+1 shell with draw loops.
Ka-Zar of the Savage Land: Bomb-uncommon — the highest-graded common/uncommon in the set. Oracle of Mul Daya on a body PLUS a growing Zabu cat = tremendous card advantage that takes over long games; opponents must kill both. 61.2% GIH / A- everywhere. Take it over most rares; a green first-pick.
Knight of Wundagore: Replaceable counters-synergy body — a {1}{G} 2/1 trample that grows once per turn when you counter another creature. 52.5% GIH and negative IWD mark it as filler; only marginally better in a GU/RG counters deck with the fight spell. Late pick.
Mister Hyde, Monster Within: A must-kill 3/2 magnet that draws or grows each upkeep — LR's B- read is closer than LLU's D+, with 55.1% GIH and a 3.7 ALSA showing steady value in a slow, grindy format. Snowballs if unchecked. A solid BG/RG role-player, better than its C- grade.
Mole Man, Moloid Master: Underwhelming rare — both LLU reviewers panned it (D+/D). A 2G 1/1 whose landfall-token engine needs graveyard-land enablement the set barely supports; you rarely get more than one Moloid. 54.4% GIH is mediocre and the body is embarrassing. A late playable at best, not a splash priority.
Pet Avengers: Fine green common but a likely non-mover — it stalls the board rather than breaks it. A 4/4 reach for four with a slow 6G power-up (counter + a 3/2 vigilance token) is stuck in the clogged four-drop slot. 57% GIH but only +0.6 IWD; good in a green deck that wants to grind, not a reason to be green.
Powerful Broker: Filler at best. A 2GG 3/3 with a late-game sorcery-speed localized proliferate does nothing without a counters payoff — the ugly 51.2% GIH, -3.1 IWD, and 20.7% play rate confirm it's a 24th-25th card. Sideboard/last-pick.
Punishing Punch: The best green removal — premium, near-catch-all. Your creature deals twice its power to a creature at instant speed, often for just G once two creatures are in the yard — a fight-you-can't-lose that scales up in BG. 59.8% GIH / +4.3 IWD / 3.2 ALSA. Guides converge B+/premium; a high pick in any green deck.
Rapid Rescue: A one-mana Seed of Hope that smooths draws — mill 2, grab a permanent, gain 2 — with a genuine live disagreement (Ethan loves it, Ben whiffed twice). The 57.8% GIH is inflated by a low 24.2% play rate (synergy/late card); needs ~35 permanents and you never want the second copy. Late-pick smoother for BG/heavy-permanent decks.
Reptil, Dinomorpher: Greater-or-garbage, and mostly garbage. A 1/2 that pays 3 or 6 mana for a one-turn stat boost is a way to lose games — enormous mana for temporary effects. 56.3% GIH looks OK but +1.3 IWD and 42% play rate reveal a below-replacement filler. Skip unless desperate for a green one-drop.
Restorative Technique: Weak fixing/lifegain — gain 2, ramp a tapped basic, and a lone +1/+1, with no board presence for its three mana. 52.5% GIH but 31% play; LLU's 'worse Rampant Growth, fixing isn't needed here' wins over Numot's 'kind of nice.' Splash-enabler only.
Rick Jones, Destined Sidekick: A 0/3 wall with a slow, capped mill-and-dig tap ability — 54.4% GIH is fine but the 14% play rate says few decks want it. Blocks well and self-mills, wanting ~10 heroes to hit; a niche role-player for a dedicated hero/graveyard build, otherwise a sideboard body.
Savage Land Dinosaur: Playable filler top-end, slightly better for BG. A 4GG 7/6 trample with basic landcycling: a real threat when you're mana-flush, a land when you're screwed, and graveyard fuel for BG. 55.2% GIH is fine for a common curve-topper; same story as all the cyclers — flexible, unexciting, always fine.
Serpent Specialist: Serviceable green one-drop, unexciting. A 1/1 deathtouch that threatens to power up to a 3/3, so the deathtouch trades up or the activation keeps blockers honest. 56.2% GIH is respectable for a common curve-filler; take it midpack, better in GU counters or as a deathtouch enabler for The Serpent Society.
Shang-Chi, Master of Kung Fu: Enabler mythic that rewards a power-up-heavy build. Giving creature abilities haste and taps for two restricted mana is strong in GU/RG counters-and-power-up decks, and opponents must respect it. But the 53% GIH is only average — it's an engine piece, not a standalone bomb.
She-Hulk, Jade Defender: Top green pickup — treat the power-up like a split card. A 3G 4/4 reach trample is already fine, and the 6-mana power-up (counter + destroy an artifact/enchantment, hitting equipment/plans/artifact creatures) adds relevant late-game reach — 60.5% GIH, +4.7 IWD. LLU B; a drafter wished for two. Prioritize it in green.
Super Strength: High-variance trap — a five-mana +4/+4 trample aura with no flash, so it's card disadvantage into any removal. The 50.5% GIH and abysmal 5.9% play rate confirm the D-; 'you'll just kill people sometimes' is the only case for it. Sideboard/omit; not a real playable.
The Thing, Ben Grimm: Absurdly large, not absurdly good. A 6-mana 7/7 trample that grows off Hero combat damage, but it's locked at six, doesn't protect itself, and is a no-evasion dummy that stalls trade. 53.1% GIH / +0.1 IWD confirm C- — worse than Ka-Zar next to it. Playable topend, not a priority.
Tigra, Feline Fury: Off-theme build-around — a flash-trample 2/1 Ajani's Pridemate that needs ~6-7 lifegain triggers the set doesn't reliably offer. 53.9% GIH and 44.4% play confirm the support isn't there; a fine flash body but rarely the payoff it wants to be.
Training Regimen: A bodyless enchantment that does too little turn-to-turn — 52.2% GIH and flat IWD confirm LR's D over LLU's charitable C-. Free counter plus trample each combat snowballs in a slow set, but with no board impact the turn it lands it's a low-priority GU/RG counters card.
The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl: Near-bomb green rare — an immediate 5/5 of stats (GGG 4/4 that Squirrels on ETB and every attack) that snowballs out of control if it untaps with the token activation. 59.8% GIH, +4.7 IWD off a 2.1 ALSA; must-kill go-wide payoff. High pick in GW/GU token/counter decks.
Undercover Skrull: Rare green praise, genuinely strong (LoL: "really good"). Two-mana ramp/fixing that taps for any color early, then becomes a 3/3 all-types once you have two creatures in the yard. 59.3% GIH with a 62.3% OH and 3.9 ALSA — versatile fixing plus a late body. A high-value common for any green deck; grab it early.
Wakandan Royal Guard: Divisive but playable green common. A 5-mana 4/4 vigilance that ETBs +1 (or +2 on a hero) can target itself for six effective stats or accelerate a hero board. The 55.5% GIH beats its D grade — a fine GW body, weakest without a counters/heroes payoff.
White Tiger, Ava Ayala: Premium green two-drop that never goes dead. A 1G 2/2 that power-ups on 6 into a counter plus a legendary 4/4 Tiger God is elite scaling — early beater, late double-body finisher. 57.4% GIH, taken at 3.8 ALSA; all guides B / top-2 green uncommon. An early pick and mana sink in any green deck.
World War Hulk: Overpriced overrun rare — free R/G creature, then +3 counters, then double-and-trample finisher, 'just an overrun with lots of ifs.' The 53.5% GIH and +1.6 IWD say it's a fine top-end but rarely the effect you need. Playable in RG when you already have a board; not a first-pick, don't overdraft it.
Abomination, Terrifying Titan: Strong RG signpost — a 4/4 trample for 4 that grows and fights, a clean two-for-one at the top of the power-up curve. 56.7% GIH / +2.1 IWD / 84% play rate back LoL's 'love this card' and the B grade. High pick for any deck with red or green; the hybrid cost makes it splashable.
Absorbing Man: Strong gold uncommon-quality rare — a {1}{G}{U} 4/4 vigilance that's already great as a beater and turns your artifacts/enchantments/lands into board impact. 59.9% GIH, +5.5 IWD, 3.4 ALSA back the B-; a high pick in GU and any Simic-adjacent deck.
Alien Invasion: A rare enchantment that pumps out an escalating haste attacker each combat — the B grade sees the ceiling, but 50.4% GIH and -0.7 IWD show it's slow and does nothing the turn it lands, and the forced-attack tokens can be bad. A build-around for a set RG board that stalls; not the reliable payoff its grade implies.
Ant-Man, Colony Commander: The GU counters signpost, but a lukewarm one — every guide found it "asks for a lot of mana and work for a minor payoff." A 3-mana 2/2 that taxes you to grow creatures and spit out 1/1s; 53.5% GIH and flat IWD confirm the mediocrity. Fine glue for the weakest pair, not a reason to be in it.
Ares, God of War: Solid BR villain rare with no guide notes but good numbers (56.3% GIH, +5.9 IWD). A 4/3 for three that must attack, but the returns-your-dying-attackers clause turns unfavorable trades into recursion and pairs with sac/ETB value. Aggressive body that rewards the villains-matter push; a strong mid pick in BR.
Armor Wars: Underwhelming UR saga — a trap. Chapter I lets opponents draw too, chapter II is a wasted cost-reducer, and chapter III's burn needs high-MV artifacts you rarely have. The sub-50% 48% GIH and 31.7% play rate confirm it's too clunky; skip it.
The Astonishing Ant-Man: Snowball engine and the GU signpost, but fragile. A GU 1/1 that grows on every draw and converts counters into an Insect swarm is a real payoff — the 60.4% OH_WR (great when you curve it out early) drives value, though the 57.3% GIH / C- reflect how a 1/1 dies to anything. Strong early pick in +1/+1 counters GU.
Avengers: Under Siege: BR bomb — makes two 2/1 menace villains, then sweeps non-villains and your opponent for 2, then Treasures out for each villain. The elite +12.3 IWD (near-best in the chunk) and 63.6% GIH across all buckets confirm the B grade is low. A one-card engine that swings the game; first-pick the BR villains deck.
Beast, Erudite Aerialist: Below-rate signpost for the weakest pair (GU counters). A 4-mana 3/3 that only flies the turn you counter it and needs to connect to draw — a lot of setup for a small payoff. 50.3% GIH / -1.8 IWD confirm both hosts' lukewarm read. Playable in GU, unexciting elsewhere.
Black Panther, Vanguard: The GW signpost and a real go-wide payoff — {2}{G}{W} 4/4 that either makes bodies or pumps the team each time a nontoken Hero enters. 55.7% GIH understates its ceiling in a dedicated heroes deck; C+ is fair but it's a strong early pick when committed to GW.
Black Widow, Double Agent: The WB signpost — a 3/2 deathtouch that makes any lone attacker effectively unblockable with first strike and menace. 55.9% GIH undersells its ceiling in a built attack-alone deck (LoL: "extremely oppressive"); the 59% play rate spreads it across non-WB decks. A strong pick when committed to white-black.
Bullseye, Death Dealer: Solid BR uncommon and a signpost-quality pick — a hybrid 2/3 that Shocks any target on ETB and repeatably thereafter, fueled by discarding/saccing artifacts. 53.8% GIH understates a card that's removal-on-a-stick in a removal-scarce format; the villain body plus reach makes it a strong BR early pick.
Captain America, Living Legend: The WU teamwork signpost and a great body (LoL: "a great monster"). A 3/4 vigilance for three that untaps each creature the first time it taps on your turn — enables tap-for-teamwork-then-attack and crews vehicles/Helicarrier then untaps the crew. 58.2% GIH; a reliable engine, high WU pick.
Cloak and Dagger, Entwined: Premium WB rare and a top signpost. Deathtouch + lifelink on a 2/2 that also exiles a card from hand or a creature (a Tidehollow Sculler that eats a threat) is exactly what the attack-alone deck wants. The 61.8% GIH / +8.1 IWD confirm a strong early pick.
The Coming of Galactus: Bomb mythic and a top BG pick — wins on its own. Chapter I removes any nonland permanent, II/III drain 4 total, IV drops a 16/16 flying trample land-destroyer — even if Galactus never lands the earlier chapters are worth it. 63.2% GIH, +11.0 IWD, 1.8 ALSA, A-. Take it near P1P1 in any black-green deck.
Daredevil, Man Without Fear: Strong RW threat — a 3/4 vigilance haste that filters your draws and swings for 5+ off hero hits, with card advantage attached. 58.3% GIH and +4.2 IWD back the B-; an aggressive body that provides value even when blocked. Premium pick for the RW/GW heroes decks, near-bomb in the right build.
Ghost, Spectral Saboteur: UB signpost — a flash 2/2 unblockable villain; provisional read (no expert notes). Guaranteed evasive damage plus flash flexibility is real in a grindy connive deck, but a vanilla 2/2 body is fragile. 52.5% GIH / +2.0 IWD / 44% play rate: a fine role-player, not a bomb. D+ grade slightly harsh.
Hulk, Gamma Goliath: The RG headliner beater — a 5-mana 6/5 reach/trample that discounts your power-ups and threatens a 9/8 trampler if unanswered. 55.1% GIH and B are solid for a top-end body; punishes durdling and anchors the Gruul curve. High pick in RG.
Iron Man, Master of Machines: The UR artifact signpost — a 1/4 flying-vigilance body that grows and draws off artifacts. 55.1% GIH is solid but conditional: a real engine only when you're committed and nobody's fighting you for it (Numot passed repeatedly). Kill it and the deck folds. Draft it as a lane-definer, not a splash.
Kang, Temporal Tyrant: The UB signpost, emblematically understated — "just a 4-mana 3/4" that connives on attack and drains on your second draw. 55.1% GIH with +4.3 IWD says it quietly accrues value and rewards a draw-two shell, but it's a grind engine, not a bomb. Good in UB, unexciting out of it.
Killmonger, Scourge of Wakanda: The best gold uncommon by far — "two gradations ahead of the pack." 2BG 3/3 that sacs a creature to destroy any nonland permanent (removal + body) and becomes a 5/4 with two creatures in yard. 60.3% GIH, splashable per Numot. The BG signpost; pivot into it and even splash it.
King T'Challa: WU teamwork bomb and a first-pick mythic. Flash 3/2 that draws a card whenever any player draws their second — an engine that snowballs in the grind — plus a transform finisher. The 61.4% GIH, +7.2 IWD, and 1.5 ALSA mark it as one of the format's best; take it every time.
The Kingpin of Crime: Strong WB grind rare — a defensive engine that also closes. A 1/5 with extort (repeatable drain in a slow format) plus an attack-trigger that lets high-toughness bodies deal combat damage as their toughness turns your wall into a clock. 56.7% GIH, +3.7 IWD, B. A premium enabler for the WB toughness/attack-alone plan.
Madame Hydra: Trap signpost — a 4-mana 2/3 that does nothing the turn it lands and needs a villain-spell density to pay off. The 49.0% GIH (sub-50) and -0.3 IWD confirm LoL's blunt 'terrible' and are the reason BR underperforms as a pair. Below replacement; only in a maxed-out villains deck, and even then reluctantly.
The Mighty Thor, Jane Foster: Premium rare, near-bomb. A 3-mana 3/3 flyer that taps down (flickers) an artifact/creature on every attack is repeatable evasive tempo, and the equipment cantrip is upside in WU/RW. 60.9% GIH / oh_wr 61.7% / ALSA 2.1 confirm it's great even from opening hand. High first-pick.
Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur: Demanding build-around — needs BOTH artifact density and second-card-draw enablers to be the 6/6 trampling card-engine it promises; Numot found Echo just better in his shell. 54.8% GIH and B reflect a card that's great in a tuned GU-artifacts deck, mediocre otherwise.
The Ruinous Wrecking Crew: A premium scalable BR bomb — 61.6% GIH, +10.8 IWD, 2.7 ALSA. Enters as an X/X with up-to-X modal ETBs (drain, edict, discard-draw, token kill) that flex from cheap value to a game-ending haymaker. Rewards villain synergy but great raw. High pick in any BR deck.
Build-around trap in most decks — 51.6% GIH, flat IWD, 27.5% play rate. A 2/2 that copies artifact activated/triggered abilities needs a dense artifact base to do anything, and the fragile body dies to everything. Only for a committed UR/artifacts deck; skip in the default 40.
The Serpent Society: Strong BG build-around rare. A 3/4 deathtouch with meaningful ward (5 poison) whose payoff — each opponent sacs a creature whenever your OTHER deathtouch creature dies — goes "absolutely savage" with instant-speed deathtouch like Widow's Bite. 57% GIH; reward it by drafting deathtouchers, otherwise a fine defensive body.
Speedball, New Warrior: Niche hybrid, underwhelming in practice. Redirecting a targeted spell and growing +2/+2 is a cute pseudo-protection/trick blank, but a 2/2 for three that needs you to target it is fragile — the sub-water 50.2% GIH and 37% play rate say it's a fringe UR playable at best.
Spider-Man, To the Rescue: Flexible GW signpost — a fine flash body with a protection ETB. Hybrid 3-drop 3/2 flash vigilance reach that can tap to give another creature indestructible blanks a removal spell or wins a combat. The -1.2 IWD is soft, but 88.4% play rate and C+ mark it as a reliable, always-playable GW glue card. Solid mid-pick.
Spider-Woman, Secret Agent: Premium WU tempo — a flash 1/4 that locks down a creature permanently, effectively hard removal on a resilient body. The 59.3% GIH, +2.9 IWD, and 95% play rate cement the B-; flexible hybrid cost makes her splashable. High pick in any white or blue deck, especially the WU teamwork shell.
Storm, Windrider: Rare with a strong body and a soft lock — a 4/4 flyer that shuts off enemy fliers, which breaks this stall-prone format. The targeted-spell flying rider is minor synergy in GW. 60.6% GIH / +6.0 IWD blow past the C+ grade; trust the live WR — this is a premium GW pick.
The Super Hero Civil War: Bomb despite the awkwardness — 69.7% GIH, +16.6 IWD, 1.6 ALSA. Steal two creatures, then an anthem, then a fight; it swings the board multiple ways over three turns. Numot's 'one of the best rares, not close.' First-pick on raw power.
Taskmaster, Mercenary Mimic: A flexible 3/5 UB rare that copies the best creature on board or in a yard each turn — a great blocker floor with a Clone ceiling. 54.8% GIH with a positive GD/OH split (56.3 vs 52.2) marks it a grind card that rewards a developed board; a solid, not premium, UB pick.
Thanos, the Mad Titan: High-ceiling splashable bomb — Numot's highlight of the run. A {R}{W}{B} 4/4 deathtouch lifelink is already a fine body, and the six-color power-up is a one-sided board wipe. The +8.3 IWD is the tell; the WUBRG(C) cost is a real build constraint, so you need fixing to unlock it. Take it and build toward it.
Thor Odinson: High-ceiling RW finisher but volatile (51.7% GIH, -0.8 IWD). A 4/4 flying vigilance double-prowess "juiced Serra Angel" that dominates if it resolves and survives — but black removal and blue bounce blank the five-mana investment easily. Take it in RW spells, but it's a build-dependent payoff, not a slam.
Titania, Rugged Rumbler: Ahead-of-curve BG beater with a real catch. A 3-mana 5/5 is enormous, but the discard-or-pay-2 tax hurts and ward 2 is its only protection. The 56.1% GIH / +3.3 IWD say it earns a slot as a curve-topper — solid uncommon, removal-dependent evaluation, take fairly early.
U.S.Agent, John Walker: Great flexible WB uncommon. Hybrid 3/2 for 3 or 4 that makes and auto-equips a +1/+2 Sturdy Shield is a clean tempo-neutral two-for-one — the shield survives the body, buffs to punch through, and feeds the equipment sub-theme. 57.6% GIH, LoL calls it "great." A high pick in WB/white; take it over most commons.
Vision Quest: UR artifacts payoff that overperforms its C+ — an X-tutor putting an artifact creature into play with X counters and haste at 4+, so it's Reanimator-meets-ramp. The 61.4% GIH and +7.3 IWD are bomb-adjacent; the gap between 56.8 OH and 64.0 GD shows it wants a target already. Slam in UR, still strong as a flexible finisher.
War Machine, Legacy of Iron: Aggressive RW role-player that underdelivers. A 1/3 flyer handing out +power each combat is only good once you've buffed it into a 2/3+; base it's a slow anthem. 51.9% GIH / -1.5 IWD undercut the LoL optimism and the C- grade. Playable in dedicated Boros aggro, mediocre otherwise.
Winter Soldier, Icy Assassin: Strong two-drop with reach — a {W}{B} 2/2 vigilance/menace that scales hard with Equipment and recurs itself with a finality counter. 59.1% GIH, +7.0 IWD, B- make it a premium WB signpost-adjacent pick; the equipment sub-theme rewards it heavily.
Wolverine, Fierce Fighter: A near-bomb — 63.9% GIH, +9.8 IWD, 2.2 ALSA. A 3/5 haste that fights on ETB is instant removal-plus-body, and the self-heal makes him nightmarish to kill in combat or trade profitably against. Slam him in any RG deck; one of the format's best rares.
Worlds Within Worlds: Trap — F grade, 2.2% play rate, effectively unplayed. A 7-mana symmetric mass-bounce-and-redeploy that resets both boards is a build-around with no home in this format. No WR data because nobody runs it; leave it in the pack.
A.I.M. Synthoids: Divisive two-drop; LLU calls it an overperformer, LoL calls it too low-impact. A 2-mana 1/3 artifact villain that surveils 2 checks a lot of synergy boxes (artifact count, villain, yard-fill) and fills the format's two-drop shortage. 52.6% GIH is modest; a fine playable in UR artifacts or BR/BG, not a high pick.
Arc Reactor: Unplayable Limited card. A 5-mana ramp rock that enters tapped and taps for colorless is a Commander card — the disastrous 43.6% GIH, -7.0 IWD, and 9.6% play rate confirm the F. Never maindeck.
Captain America's Shield: Sneaky-premium colorless equipment — moved way up. Indestructible, +0/+8, vigilance, and taps a blocker on attack makes any creature (especially a flyer) an oppressive recurring threat only exile answers. 57.4% GIH but 96% play rate and 1.5 ALSA show everyone takes it; Numot got blown out by it. Colorless, so grab it in any deck.
Cosmic Cube: Free-spell engine whose stats are elite (61.5% GIH, +7.4 IWD, 1.4 ALSA, 97% play rate) precisely because you first-pick it and build around big attackers. The D grade is stale pre-data pessimism — it's a colorless bomb in any board-dominant deck; cast a spell off the top ≤ your biggest attacker's power each swing. Take it early.
Dependable Quinjet: Fixing filler, near-unplayable on rate. Crew 4 is brutally steep and this format doesn't demand a mana-rock/vehicle; it's cuttable once you have real fixing. 53.7% GIH / 33% play rate confirm the D read. Take only for a greedy multicolor 'soup' deck, then cut it.
H.E.R.B.I.E. Scout Unit: High-floor colorless glue — a 4-mana 2/1 flyer that cantrips and sometimes ramps, going in nearly any deck. 58.1% GIH and 82.5% play back Mark's 'every deck' over Alex's '23rd-card'; a reliable role-player, best in lower-ceiling/aggressive builds per LoL.
Iron Man Armor: A premium colorless equipment — 58.6% GIH, 1.3 ALSA and 97.7% play rate mean everyone takes it. Auto-attaches for +2/+1 and flying (evasion is the format's tiebreaker), and can animate itself into a threat. Great in any deck, artifacts or not; an early pick regardless of colors.
S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier: Divisive but a fine WU/blue playable — Alex ran it over pushback and it held its C. A 4-mana 4/5 flyer that brings two 1/1 soldiers is a flyer-plus-value package (vehicles with tokens are underrated), and it goes broken with Captain America. 55.8% GIH; crew 6 is a real cost, so it wants a body-heavy deck.
Super-Adaptoid: Fine colorless role-player, plays in any deck. Power = your legendary count (usually a 2/2-3/3 given how legend-dense MSH is) and it steals a keyword on every ETB/attack. 57.2% GIH at 2.0 ALSA with 94% play — reliably a solid body that gets better in a legends-heavy build. Good utility pick, not a bomb.
The Ten Rings: Trap mythic. An 8-mana artifact that sets hand size to ten and refills you decks you out and does nothing to the board for eight mana — the sub-50% 48.2% GIH and D- grade confirm it. Effectively a non-card in Limited.
Ultron, Artificial Malevolence: Build-around mythic that shines late in UR artifacts, mediocre elsewhere. A 3-mana 2/4 that copies your artifacts (animating noncreatures as 2/2s) is scary with fuel but hard to power on curve — 53.6% GIH, +0.9 IWD despite a 1.9 ALSA (taken on name). Colorless body goes anywhere, but it's a payoff, not a bomb. Mid pick.
Ultron Drone: Bingo-space filler — a 3-mana 2/3 artifact villain with an expensive power-up to a 4/5 plus a 2/2 token. The 53.6% GIH but low 32.0% play rate mark it as replaceable body that ticks artifact/villain boxes. Fine last-few-cards inclusion in UR/BR; the power-up is a mana sink you'll rarely afford.
Vibranium Energy Daggers: Trap — colorless equipment that this equipment-poor format doesn't reward. +2/+2 for equip-3 is too slow and there aren't enough payoffs. 50.3% GIH / -0.5 IWD / 14% play rate confirm D-. Indestructible is nearly irrelevant. Skip.
The Vision: Colorless bomb-adjacent and near-universal — 98.9% play, 1.2 ALSA, 59.3% GIH. A 4-mana 2/5 flyer/vigilance that turns every noncreature spell into double strike, indestructibility, or a card. Alex would first-pick it; a splashless slam in any deck.
Viv Vision, Teen Synthezoid: A 3-mana 2/2 flyer that only draws at power 4+, with an expensive power-up 7 — the 53.6% GIH and D+ grade agree there are too few cheap boosts to turn it on reliably. The evasion keeps it playable filler; take it as a colorless flyer, don't count on the draw.
A.I.M. Labs: Fine fixing land for UB — enters tapped, gains a life, taps for U or B. 56.0% GIH and +2.2 IWD are strong for a dual land, reflecting how much this slow format values fixing and the lifegain buffer. Auto-include in UB and a fine early pick to enable splashes.
Asgardian Citadel: Solid RW fixing land. Enters tapped, gains a life, taps for R/W — the tempo hit is real but the fixing plus incidental lifegain smooths any Boros build. 56.4% GIH and 63% play; a routine include in two-color RW decks. Take when you need fixing, not over playables.
Avengers Hangar: Solid WU fixing land — play as many as your deck wants. Enters tapped but gains a life and fixes both colors; 57.7% GIH shows the fixing is worth the tempo hit in a two-color deck. A reliable early inclusion for teamwork/control builds.
Avengers Tower: Best of the utility lands — nearly a free include. Taps for hero-only any-color fixing and, for 4, digs 3 for a hero at instant speed; since almost everything is a hero you rarely need more than 7-9. 60.2% GIH from a land is excellent grind value in board stalls. D+ badly underrates it — play it in most decks.
Baxter Building: The format's most impressive stall-breaker — a fixing land that's effectively '4, tap, draw a card' given the set's ubiquitous 4-toughness bodies, plus any-color filtering for bombs. Both LoL and Numot revised it up (Numot kept forgetting the draw mode); the 57.4% GIH and 84% play rate crush LR's F. A free, high-value land slot; don't sleep on it.
Birnin Zana Plaza: Fine fixing for GW — a tapland that gains a life and taps for G or W. Nothing exciting, but two-color fixing plus incidental life is a real inclusion in the go-wide heroes deck. 56.7% GIH / oh_wr 58.8% reflect the decks that play it, not raw power. Playable land, C-grade correct.
Castle Doom: Below-rate utility land — the mana is fine but the {3}+sac Doombot mode is slow, and 52.6% GIH with a negative OH_WR shows it can cost you early tempo. D- is harsh but it's a marginal include for artifact-heavy UR/mono-artifact decks only.
Dark Fortress: A strong BR fixing land — enters untapped, taps for C freely and B/R with a trivial condition (basic land or same-turn), so it's nearly a dual with no drawback. 54.5% GIH and C+ grade; a fine early pick to smooth a BR villains manabase.
Fisk Tower: Fine WB fixing land — tapped, gain 1, taps for W or B. 55.5% GIH shows the format rewards fixing; the lifegain matters in grindy games. Solid include in WB (and splash-enabling elsewhere); take it when you're in those colors or hedging a splash.
Gathering Place: Above-rate GW fixing land (C+ grade, 56.3% GIH). Taps for colorless always, or G/W if it entered this turn or you control a basic — so it's untapped fixing in practice, unlike the tapped duals. Low opportunity cost in GW heroes; a comfortable include and a mild pick-up in the late pack.
