Gleaming Bastion: Premium dual land — near-free WU fixing. Taps for colorless always, or W/U with a trivial basic-land condition, with essentially no downside. The 57.3% GIH / +0.8 IWD and 3.9 ALSA reflect that mana-fixing this clean is a high pick for any UW deck.
Hell's Kitchen: Solid BR fixing land — a fine include in the villains pair. Enters tapped, gains 1 life, taps for B or R; unremarkable but the 54.7% GIH and 59.9% play rate confirm it does its job smoothing a two-color aggro/midrange mana base. No downside beyond the tapland tempo. Auto-include in BR, low-opportunity-cost pick.
Hidden Lair: Strong fixing land for UB — taps for colorless always and U/B when you control a basic (trivially met), so it's near-untapped dual mana with no real downside. The 56.6% GIH and +3.9 IWD back the C+; painless fixing that helps you play the best pair in the format. Always run it in a UB or splashing deck.
Los Diablos Missile Base: Fine RG fixing — a tapland gaining a life, tapping for R or G. Slots into the ramp/power-up deck to smooth double colors; the ETB tap is a real cost in an aggressive shell. 55.8% GIH is a deck-selection artifact, not power. Solid inclusion when you're in these colors.
Pym Technologies: Perfectly fine dual for GU — enters tapped, gains a life, taps for G or U. 56.5% GIH and C are exactly what a fixing land should be; take it when you're in Simic and want smoother mana, otherwise a late playable.
Stark Industries: A tapland dual for UR that gains 1 life — the enters-tapped clause is why 56.1% GIH pairs with a late 6.2 ALSA. Fine fixing for the UR artifact deck and playable filler elsewhere, but the tempo cost keeps it a mid-to-late pick.
Subterranean Cavern: Fine BG fixing land — tapped, gain 1, taps for B or G. 56.5% GIH is the best of the taplands here, fitting the grindy BG graveyard deck that wants to hit land drops and gain life. Auto-include in BG; a low-opportunity-cost pickup that smooths and enables splashes.
Surveillance Room: Underrated fixing land — Mark plays the first in every deck. The F grade is stale; the 56.6% GIH and 82% play rate tell the real story. Surveil 1 on ETB plus any-color filtering (for 1) enables splashes like Killmonger even when you're not planning to splash. Ignore the letter; take it as free fixing.
Training Compound: The RG version of the clean dual — strong fixing with negligible cost. Colorless anytime, R/G under an easy basic condition. The 55.4% GIH confirms it's a smooth include; grab it for any Gruul power-up/ramp deck.
Villainous Hideout: Real value land for heavy-villain decks, least-good of the utility trio. Colorless/villain-only fixing plus a 3-mana repeatable connive-a-villain engine grinds card selection in board stalls — 57.5% GIH, +4.0 IWD in the right deck (e.g. BR). Run it when your villain count supports it; a fine but not focal pickup.
Archangel of Thune: Provisional (null text): the real Archangel is a five-mana 3/4 flying lifelink that snowballs the board with +1/+1 counters on every lifegain — a hard bomb. The 1.6 ALSA and 96.3% play rate scream slam-and-win; missing WR is a Scryfall gap, not weakness. First-pick it in any white deck.
Concerted Effort: Provisional (Scryfall gap; no text, stats, or grade). This is the classic keyword-sharing white enchantment — a build-around that needs evasion/keyword creatures to matter and does nothing on an empty board. ALSA 4.0 / 28.8% play rate suggest a fringe, hopeful pick. Treat as sideboard build-around.
Don't Move: White mythic sorcery, text missing from Scryfall so this read is provisional — but a 3.1 ALSA and 74.6% play rate signal a high-impact card drafters take early and run readily. Treat as a premium white pick until the text confirms otherwise.
Ephemerate: Null text (Scryfall gap) — this is the classic 1-mana blink-with-rebound instant, a premium enabler that reuses ETB creatures (Hero in Training, Madame Masque, Wolverine) and dodges removal. No WR data, but 67% play rate and its pedigree make this a strong white pick; read provisional.
Final Showdown: Provisional read (null oracle text): a white mythic instant with a strong 2.3 ALSA and 87% play rate, so the population treats it as a premium, near-always-maindecked answer or combat blowout. Numbers point to a high pick in white; grab it and confirm the text in-game.
Light of Promise: Null oracle text (Scryfall gap) — provisional read. A white mythic Aura with only 7% play rate and 5.6 ALSA, so it's seeing almost no maindeck use; likely a narrow buildaround or Constitution-style lifegain aura that doesn't translate to Limited. Treat as sideboard/filler until you read the actual card.
Path to Exile: Bonus-sheet premium removal — one-mana exile any creature. No MSH-specific WR (null stats), but the 2.1 ALSA and 90.8% play rate show it's picked and played near-universally. Best white removal you can open; take it over almost anything and eat the land you give.
Return to the Ranks: Provisional read (Scryfall text gap): the historical card is a WW reanimation sorcery that returns X small creatures with convoke — a go-wide GW payoff. The 15.7% play rate and 4.9 ALSA say most drafters leave it in the sideboard; it needs a critical mass of cheap heroes to earn its slot. Niche build-around, low priority.
Righteous Fury: Provisional (null text/grade): a white mythic sorcery taken early (3.0 ALSA) and played in 68.5% of white decks, which points to a real payoff, likely a wide-board or damage swing. Lean bomb-adjacent on the pick position; treat as a high pick in aggressive white until stats fill in.
Steelshaper's Gift: Provisional (Scryfall gap). A 1-mana tutor for an Equipment — only as good as your best equipment, and this format's equipment is weak (see Vibranium Daggers). 10.7% play rate is the tell: almost no one runs it. Sideboard/unplayable unless you have a standout equipment target.
Teferi's Protection: White mythic instant, text unavailable (provisional read). The classic Teferi's Protection is a powerful blowout/fog effect; the 3.9 ALSA and 50.6% play suggest a situational-but-respected card. Likely a strong-but-niche pick in white; verify the effect in-client.
Counterspell: Null text, but this is the iconic UU hard counter — 87.6% play rate shows nearly every blue deck runs it. Unconditional interaction is premium in a slow grindy format where answering a bomb wins the game. A high blue pick; read provisional on the Scryfall gap.
Cyberdrive Awakener: Provisional read (null text): a blue mythic artifact Construct with a 3.1 ALSA and 60.5% play rate — picked early and run often, so the population rates it a real threat, likely a payoff for the artifact/vehicle theme. Treat as a high blue pick pending the actual text.

Harbinger of the Seas: Provisional read — null text and near-zero data (3.8% play rate, 5.8 ALSA). This is the Islands-produce-only-U merfolk; a strong constructed hatebear but a nearly blank body in Limited with no relevant targets. Treat as unplayable filler here.

Final Act: Provisional (Scryfall gap), but the 68.2% play rate and ALSA 2.8 flag it as a real, early-drafted black card — most likely a big removal/wrath-style payoff. Prioritize as premium black removal on the data alone; grab it high and let the read firm up.
Massacre Girl: Black mythic, text missing (provisional) — but the pedigree (a chaining team-wipe assassin) plus a 2.3 ALSA and 84.3% play rate flag a genuine bomb drafters grab early. Treat as a high pick in black until the oracle text confirms.
No Mercy: Null text (Scryfall gap) — the classic black enchantment that destroys any creature that deals combat damage to you, a hard fog-plus-removal wall. No WR data and a null play rate, but historically a strong defensive rare for grindy control. Read provisional; likely a solid B/UB pick.

Fiery Emancipation: Null oracle text; this is the classic triple-damage enchantment for six-plus. Only 33% play rate says it's a top-end mythic that many decks can't support or don't want at that cost. A splashy finisher in aggressive red, but slow for a grindy format — a build-dependent payoff, not a reliable slam. Provisional read.
Fury of the Horde: Provisional — null text, and the data (5.2 ALSA, 16.6% play rate) says it's rarely played. The free extra-combat sorcery (exile two red cards to cast) needs a dedicated aggressive shell; in this slow format it's a niche finisher at best. Low priority.

Seize the Day: Provisional (null text): the real Seize the Day is a red sorcery granting an extra combat with flashback — a strong finisher in an aggressive board. Null play rate and 4.0 ALSA leave the read thin; treat as a role-player/finisher in RW aggro pending data, not a premium pick.
Bedlam: Provisional (Scryfall gap). The old red enchantment that forbids blocking — a symmetric all-out-attack effect that's a narrow, dangerous build-around, not a maindeck card. 6.6% play rate confirms almost no one wants it. Sideboard/trap; leave it.
Beast Within: Green mythic instant, no text or stats (provisional) — the classic Beast Within is premium catch-all removal (destroy any permanent, give a 3/3). In a removal-scarce format that's a slam; treat as a top-tier green pick pending confirmation of the reprint.
Defense of the Heart: Null text, but this is the green enchantment that, if an opponent has 3+ creatures at your upkeep, fetches two creatures from your library onto the battlefield — a bomb-tutor that's live in a slow board-stall format. 56.3% play rate. No WR data; read provisional but promising in RG/GW.
Force of Vigor: Provisional read (null text): a green mythic instant with a middling 5.1 ALSA and low 19.2% play rate — historically a free-if-you-pitch-a-green-card artifact/enchantment blowout, which is narrow in Limited. Mostly a sideboard card against artifact/Web Up decks; maindeck filler at best.

Read as a strong green trick that saves your board and blanks removal; provisional pending the tile.

Black Panther, Wakandan King: Provisional read (null text) but clearly a bomb — the GW heroes-matter signpost with a 2.4 ALSA and 85% play rate, picked early and near-always played. The go-wide heroes payoff every GW drafter wants; take it very highly and confirm the text in-game.
Captain America, First Avenger: Null oracle text (Scryfall gap) — a WUR mythic legend. Escape to the Wilds: Provisional read on null text, but the numbers point to a solid RG value engine (4.2 ALSA, 60.6% play rate). It's the impulse-five-cards-plus-extra-land sorcery — real card advantage and ramp for the grindy Gruul deck. Take it as a good midrange payoff.
Fight to the Death: Provisional read (text gap): a RW instant, likely a bidirectional/multi-fight combat effect. The tiny 10.2% play rate and 5.3 ALSA say drafters overwhelmingly pass it — situational, needs a board you're ahead on. Treat it as a sideboard/niche card in RW, not a maindeck pick.
